extracted.intended_audience: federal agency staff, regulatory/legal professionals, and members of the public interested in federal information-collection requirements and compliance with the Paperwork Reduction Act
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and statutory requirements for federal agencies to lawfully design, publish, and obtain approval for information collections from the public under the Paperwork Reduction Act (PRA). Focuses on what agencies must include, consult on, and obtain from OMB/OIRA before imposing paperwork burdens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determine specific objective for collection
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency must determine a specific objective met by the collection of information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should identify the concrete purpose(s) for which the information is being gathered (statutory citation in article: 44 U.S.C. §§ 3501–3521). This requirement is the statutory starting point for any proposed reporting or recordkeeping requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop a plan for use of the information
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency must develop a plan for how the collected information will be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plans should explain intended uses and how the information supports agency functions; the PRA expects agencies to specify practical utility and usage, not merely collect information without an articulated plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test collection method (pilot testing when appropriate)
rubrics_metrics.description: In some cases, agencies must test the collection method through a pilot program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pilot testing is recommended/required where appropriate to validate methods, assess burden, and improve clarity or functionality before full implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forms must explain purposes of the information collection
rubrics_metrics.description: Forms must include an explanation to the audience of the purposes of the information collection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statutory and implementing guidance require that respondents be informed why the information is being requested so they understand the collection's purpose and utility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forms must estimate the paperwork burden
rubrics_metrics.description: Forms must include an estimate of the paperwork burden imposed on respondents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must provide an estimate of the time/effort burden; PRA and OMB review evaluate the reasonableness and accuracy of burden estimates (see cited 44 U.S.C. and OMB guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Forms must state whether response is voluntary
rubrics_metrics.description: Forms must indicate whether responding to the information collection is voluntary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should clearly state whether responses are mandatory or voluntary and cite authority when responses are required by statute/regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish Federal Register notice and allow at least 60 days for public comment
rubrics_metrics.description: In most cases, agencies are required to publish notice of a proposed requirement in the Federal Register and allow at least 60 days for public comments on the need for and burden of the requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 60-day public comment period solicits input on necessity, burden estimates, clarity, and burden-minimization; agencies must consider comments when finalizing collections (statutory citation: 44 U.S.C. §3506(c) and related text).

rubrics_metrics.name: Obtain OMB control number (approval) before promulgation
rubrics_metrics.description: All federal agencies must receive approval from OMB—in the form of a 'control number'—before promulgating a paper form, website, survey or electronic submission that will impose an information collection burden on the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No collection that imposes more than minimal identification requirements should be implemented without the assigned control number; this is a precondition to lawful collection under the PRA (statutory citation: 44 U.S.C. §3507(a)(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'burden' for PRA purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'burden' is defined as anything beyond 'that necessary to identify the respondent, the date, the respondent's address, and the nature of the instrument.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This statutory definition limits PRA coverage to substantive information collections and excludes minimal administrative identifiers; agencies should apply this definition when determining whether PRA clearance is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: No penalty for failing to comply without valid control number
rubrics_metrics.description: No person may be penalized for refusing an information collection request that does not display a valid control number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must ensure collections display the valid OMB control number; absence of a valid control number negates enforcement against respondents (statutory citation: 44 U.S.C. §3512(a)(1) and §3507(g)).

rubrics_metrics.name: OMB approval duration and renewal interval
rubrics_metrics.description: Once obtained, OMB approval (control number) must be renewed every three years and may not be approved for a period in excess of 3 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should track approval expirations and submit renewals in a timely manner (statutory citation: 44 U.S.C. §3507(g)).

rubrics_metrics.name: OIRA/OMB centralized review and Information Collection Budget
rubrics_metrics.description: The PRA makes OIRA into a centralized clearinghouse for all government forms, enabling assessment of the overall impact of government information collections; OIRA publishes an annual Information Collection Budget.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OIRA oversight allows government-wide measurement of mandatory paperwork burden (historical counts cited: ~9.7 billion hours in 2009 and 2016). Agencies should expect centralized scrutiny and inclusion of approved collections in the annual Collection Budget.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory public consultation objectives (four evaluation goals)
rubrics_metrics.description: When soliciting public comment, agencies must obtain input to: (i) evaluate whether the proposed collection is necessary for proper performance of agency functions (practical utility); (ii) evaluate accuracy of the agency's estimate of burden; (iii) enhance the quality, utility, and clarity of the information to be collected; and (iv) minimize the burden on respondents, including through automated techniques or other information technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These four consultation objectives (quoted/paraphrased from 44 U.S.C. §3506(c)(2)(A) and related subsections) define what useful public comments should address and guide agency responses to comments and design changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: 1995 amendment: scope includes information provided to the public
rubrics_metrics.description: The Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995 confirmed that OIRA's authority extended over not only agency orders to provide information to the government, but also agency orders to provide information to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must treat public-facing information collections (not only reports to government) as within PRA clearance requirements; this expands the kinds of instruments requiring control numbers and scrutiny.
